metric: Pairs decided from SQL and column names alone: 889 proved equivalent, 1874 proved different by a counterexample database, 37 unknown. All 2,800 pairs are also in VeriEQL's LeetCode set, which keeps the keys these files drop.
caveats: Rewrite rules were written while looking at these pairs; the held-out fifth was reserved partway through, so it is a weak check. The published labels assume LeetCode's keys and NOT NULL rules, which the files omit, so 476 pairs labelled equivalent get a valid counterexample here. Data is downloaded from a pinned commit (no licence file, not bundled). The October counterexample-search changes (seed per pair, duplicate rows, three-decimal values, date and divisor neighbours) were developed on dev pairs only; the held-out fifth was not inspected. The outer-join flattening rules (outer_join_flatten.py) were developed on dev pairs only. The structural aggregate rules were developed on dev pairs only. The set-split rules (set_split_rules.py, #389) were developed on dev pairs only (failing-tests cluster 11, all 72 dev). The ABS(x - y) facts and the x <> y split (#403) were developed on dev pairs only (cluster 11, 5 dev pairs). Measured on master 30eb0cb, after #403. One pair that compares a string with a number moved from unknown to unsupported when the provers began declining such comparisons (#542, #547); the score and the 862 proofs are unchanged. One more pair (a COALESCE that returns a string for a NULL and a number otherwise, compared with a number) moved from proved to unsupported when kinds began to be inferred from the query (#613): the proof was right on MySQL by luck ('SOME BOGUS VALUE' reads as 0) but rested on a string never equalling a number; the pair is a dev pair. One more pair moved from unknown to unsupported when kinds began to follow SELECT * and set operations: the score and the 861 proofs are unchanged. The pairs carry no column types, so the harness now declares each column the queries compare with a string as text, the same reading its counterexample search uses; without it the new untyped-column check (#613) would decline 17 proofs that compare two different product-name strings, 4 of them held out (no pair was inspected, the check was found from the proof counts alone). The score and the 861 proofs are unchanged. Re-measured on 2026-11-10 on main c384968 before any change: 2734/2800, 0 wrong (860 proved; one proof fewer than the 2026-10-03 record, not traced), held-out fifth 560/580. Six rule modules were then written against the 46 undecided development pairs (case_arm_rules.py, unmatched_outer_join.py, having_count_rules.py, grouped_self_membership.py, disjoint_union.py, semijoin_shapes.py), developed on dev pairs only: 24 of them now prove, and the held-out fifth goes from 560 to 565 with no proof lost, measured on commit e904d62. Exposure of the held-out fifth during that work: a subagent once ran tests/test_singh_bedathur_benchmark.py, which runs every pair, for about 30 minutes; its output was not read. A first version of the counted-key rule lost one held-out proof; the loss was found from the counts and fixed by switching rules off on that pair (verdict only) and trying made-up spellings of COUNT(k) > 1, without reading the pair. A stricter reading of bare column names in the string-type guard needs the schema's column lists to keep the proofs of this harness, which declares only text columns; the harness already passes them.
correctness: 0 wrong: every proof re-checked on 900 random DuckDB databases; every 'different' carries a database on which DuckDB returns different bags (numbers compared as rounded floats, fractions exact in binary)
held_out: 565/580, 0 wrong (held-out fifth, by hash of the pair)
